title: Pointwise quasi-finiteness of schemes is invariant under arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $b:T^{\prime}\to T$ be any morphism of schemes. Form $X^{\prime}=X\times_TT^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $a:X^{\prime}\to X$ and $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$. For every $x^{\prime}\in X^{\prime}$, the morphism $f^{\prime}$ is quasi-finite at $x^{\prime}$ if and only if $f$ is quasi-finite at $a(x^{\prime})$, using the pointwise scheme notion [pqf-def-quasifinite]. No flatness, surjectivity, finite-type, separatedness, or Noetherian hypothesis on $b$ is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], $f^{\prime}$ is locally of finite type. For either $(h:Z\to B,z)=(f,a(x^{\prime}))$ or $(f^{\prime},x^{\prime})$, choose an affine open $V\subset B$ about $h(z)$ and then an affine open $U\subset h^{-1}(V)$ about $z$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Write $R=\mathcal O_B(V)$, $A=\mathcal O_Z(U)$, and let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ correspond to $z$. The induced map $R\to A$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs].

For each of these chosen pairs, $h$ is quasi-finite at $z$ if and only if $R\to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$. Indeed, the forward direction first gives isolation of the point of $Z_{h(z)}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated]; [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] then gives quasi-finiteness for the chosen affine pair. Conversely, this finite-type affine pair is exactly a witness in [pqf-def-quasifinite].

Put $\mathfrak p=(R\to A)^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension], quasi-finiteness of $R\to A$ at $\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to dimension zero at the corresponding point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. By [lem-sbc-affine-coordinate-fibre-dimension], this is dimension zero in the fibre of $U\to V$ at $z$ (the tensor factors may be interchanged by $a\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes a$). By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], that fibre is an open neighbourhood of the distinguished point in $Z_{h(z)}$, compatibly with its projection. Dimension at a point agrees on an open neighbourhood by [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]: intersect any ambient neighbourhood with this open, and conversely regard its open neighbourhoods as ambient opens. Thus the criterion in step 2 is equivalent to $\dim_z Z_{h(z)}=0$.

source.place: Tag 01TM (1), reduction to affine opens; Tag 0397 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0), second proof; Algebra Tag 00PJ (lemma-isolated-point), (1) iff (4).

proof.text: For $x=a(x^{\prime})$, $t^{\prime}=f^{\prime}(x^{\prime})$ and $t=b(t^{\prime})=f(x)$, [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] gives $\dim_{x^{\prime}} X^{\prime}_{t^{\prime}}=\dim_x X_t$. Therefore the dimension-zero conditions obtained in steps 2--3 for $f^{\prime}$ and $f$ are equivalent. This is the required equivalence at $x^{\prime}$. The dimension comparison allows arbitrary $b$; none of the preceding steps added a hypothesis on $b$.
